safety_lead_time.comparison_action: REDUCE: SAP safety lead time of 0.0 days is already at minimum; recommend setting safety stock to 2,582 units in ERP

narrative: Material PL3__MF2AB007 exhibits a lumpy demand pattern with a mean of 1,395 units/day and CV of 0.61, driven by recurring zero-demand days interspersed with high-volume production days. Lead times are very short (mean 1.05 days) but highly variable (CV 0.89), making lead-time variability the dominant buffer driver at 69% of total variance. The (r,Q) policy with MOQ-constrained order quantity of 22,835 units and safety stock of 2,582 units achieves 95% service level while reducing the current ERP safety stock by 97%, releasing substantial working capital. The storage constraint at 124,599 units is non-binding at 20.4% utilisation.
warnings: EOQ raw (5,058) is below MOQ (22,835); order quantity set to MOQ.
SAP safety stock (81,555) is 31.6x the analytically derived value (2,582) — significant over-buffering detected.
Capacity utilisation is 20.4%; no capacity constraint binding.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The material has short, predictable lead times and predominantly high-volume demand with intermittent zero days. The (r,Q) policy is optimal: it triggers a fixed replenishment of MOQ=22,835 units when on-hand stock falls to the reorder point of 4,698 units, balancing ordering frequency against holding cost while the MOQ constraint governs order sizing rather than EOQ.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The MOQ (22,835) significantly exceeds EOQ (5,058), implying over-ordering relative to the economic optimum. However, the storage capacity (124,599 units) is not binding, so this does not create a physical constraint. The high MOQ inflates cycle stock and holding cost but is supplier-driven and cannot be reduced without renegotiation.
